mentions.name: GridWhale
mentions.description: GridWhale is a vertically-integrated, cloud-based development and execution environment that eliminates the complexity of assembling many dependencies. It provides a platform abstraction layer over the distributed system, so a program runs as if it were on a single big abstract machine with direct access to input, output, and storage, while the platform handles the underlying distributed complexity.
mentions.problem: Modern programs run on distributed systems with thousands/millions of clients connecting to hundreds/thousands of backend servers, forcing developers to deal with client-server communications, async storage calls, and idempotent microservice requests instead of focusing on their programs.
mentions.audience: Modern programs run on distributed systems with thousands/millions of clients connecting to hundreds/thousands of backend servers, forcing developers to deal with client-server communications, async storage calls, and idempotent microservice requests instead of focusing on their programs.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm still working on GridWhale.

My premise is simple: What if we could build a vertically-integrated, batteries-included, cloud-based development and execution environment that eliminated all the complexity of cobbling together a hundred different dependencies?
